page.layout: One printed page (folio 412), with marginal notes in the left margin. Running head across the top: "LIBRI IV." at centre and "De bellis" at right. Text in one column, top to bottom: the end of a paragraph from the previous page, a chapter heading, then a new paragraph that runs to the foot. Left margin: four notes beside the first paragraph and one note beside the second. The right edge shows a sliver of the facing page, which is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Mulctam in eodem hoc casu quare non pater, sed judex definiat.cum sententia & æstimatione solvere tenetur, adeoque judicum erat definire, quid numeran-dum esset. Fieri enim facile potest, ut modum maritus excedat, & circumstantias, ex iracundiæ calore, affectuumque fervore, ponderare minus queat. Unde videmus, etiam in pœnis fontium publicis, privatæ vindictæ cupiditatem procul facessere, neque odiis indulgere nos debere, si ab illis læsi, aut quacunque ratione injuria affecti, vimque injustam passi simus: sed commiseratione potius fontes, & qui plectuntur prosequendos. Quemadmodum ipse etiam magistratus eodem animo supplicia capitalia exsequi debet. Neque enim publica reorum supplicia privatæ cujusquam libidini servire debent. Manifestum autem ex his omnibus est, legem hanc moralem esse, ut quæ cum jure naturæ undequaque convenit, & tam in Canonico, quàm Civili jure repetita exstat.
main_text.head: CAPUT XVI. De bellis.
main_text.p: QUæ præcedentibus duobus capitibus tractata sunt, ad vindictam privatam, legibus, sexti præcepti Decalogi appendicibus, prohibitam, referuntur. Sequuntur leges ad publicam vindictam, quæ magistratus est, exercendam, & quæ circa hanc ratio atque modus observanda sint, Bellum quid.pertinentes. Vindicta autem hæc in bellis sita est, & exercetur, quæ necessaria sunt adversus publicam vim, defensio; vel pœna justa, propter atroces injurias, quæ armata manu ab or-dina.

page.notes: The right-hand edge shows part of the facing page; it is not transcribed. The marginal note "Mulctam" is read as "Mulctam" from a ct ligature that looks like "ft" at this resolution; the word is uncertain. The text is cut off at the foot; "dina." is the last printed line. No catchword or signature is visible. The text is clear enough to transcribe, but the scan is small and some ligatures are doubtful.
